title: Vigil demands justice ; Family wants inquest into shooting death
article: The family of an Aylmer man shot and killed two years ago by a police officer as he stood in his driveway is threatening legal action against the officer and the City of Gatineau.
An Aylmer police officer clubbed, pepper-sprayed and then fired three bullets at close range into David Leclair during an attempted arrest at the 35-year-old's Conroy St. home on June 28, 2008.
Leclair, who was unarmed, was killed while horrified family members looked on in what they are calling a clear case of police brutality.

The Surete du Quebec conducted their own four-month investigation into the shooting, before the Quebec Crown attorney's office announced in February 2009 that no charges would be pursued against the officer.

The officer, Pierre-Francois Blais, was trying to arrest Leclair at his home following an alleged domestic complaint from Leclair's then-girlfriend when three shots were fired, striking Leclair in the torso and arm.
He died eight hours later in hospital after a priest administered last rites.

At a vigil Sunday commemorating the second anniversary of Leclair's death, family members repeated their call for a public inquiry into Leclair's death, after the Minister of Public Security's office informed the family earlier in June that no such inquiry would happen.

"We will not stop or give up in our quest for justice," said Leclair's sister Donna Leclair, saying if no public inquiry is launched within months, "we will lodge a civil suit against the police officer responsible for the shooting and the City of Gatineau."
Meanwhile, family members say the painful memories of Leclair's death linger for the large family, where David was the youngest of nine siblings.

"This is how we live day in, day out for the last two years. It's destroyed our lives," said sister Cindy, who now cares for her slain brother's daughter, 11-year-old Britney, who she said has been "traumatized" by the shooting.
"She has her breakdowns," she said of Britney, who was too distraught to attend the vigil. "She talks about him all the time. She feels bad that she never got to say goodbye."
